newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cuts loopholes in new import credit rules.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cuts loopholes in new import credit rules.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank on Wednesday said it had taken steps to close loopholes in import financing restrictions it imposed last month.

The new rules, announced on March 26, require importers using financing of 360 days or less to pay for their foreign currency used in credit contracts on the day they pick up their goods from the warehouse.
Jose Maria Carvalho, who heads the Central Bank's foreign exchange department, said many importers were simply extending their financing contracts to avoid the new rules.
Carvalho said now the rule would apply on the first 360 days of all import financing operations, no matter how long the term of the credit contract.
"We want to create the same rules for all importers," Carvalho told a news conference.

In addition, the Central Bank defined specifically what it meant by petroleum derivative products, which were exempted from the March 26 rules. Carvalho said importers were claiming the exemption, saying plastic tables and textiles were made from petroleum by-products.
